questions.stem: State the wave family of light and the drawing style used for it.
questions.modelAnswer: Light is a transverse (electromagnetic) wave, drawn as a wavy line with peaks and troughs.

questions.stem: State the two boundary behaviours of light named in the note.
Explain why light is drawn as a transverse wave rather than with compression lines.
questions.modelAnswer: Light belongs to the electromagnetic spectrum, and all EM waves are transverse, so the peak-and-trough drawing shows its crosswise vibration while compression lines would falsely suggest a longitudinal push-pull wave.

questions.stem: A camera flash reflects off a window into a driver’s eyes, and the same beam bends as it passes into the glass. Identify each behaviour and the wave family involved.
questions.modelAnswer: The bounce at the window is reflection and the bend on entering the glass is refraction; both happen to light, a transverse electromagnetic wave.

questions.stem: State the wave family of sound and its everyday reflected form.
questions.modelAnswer: Sound is a longitudinal wave; its reflection is heard as an echo.

questions.stem: State how rarefactions appear on a longitudinal wave diagram.
questions.modelAnswer: Rarefactions appear as lines drawn further apart, showing the spread-out regions.

questions.stem: Explain why the drawing styles for light and sound differ.
questions.modelAnswer: Light is transverse so its crosswise vibration is drawn as a peak-and-trough line, while sound is longitudinal so its along-the-line push-pull is drawn as bunched and spaced lines; each style encodes the true vibration direction of its family.

questions.stem: A swimmer clicks two stones together underwater and hears the click reflected from the pool wall. Identify the wave family, the reflected sound and one behaviour the click shares with light at the water surface.
questions.modelAnswer: The click is a longitudinal sound wave; its wall reflection is an echo; at the water surface the click also refracts, bending between media just as light does.
